findings.title: Logout DoS via unsigned JWT (jwt.decode instead of jwt.verify)
findings.description: POST /api/v1/auth/logout used jwt.decode() (no signature verification). Any attacker with any valid-looking JWT structure could force-revoke all refresh tokens for an arbitrary userId, effectively locking users out of their sessions.
findings.impact: Denial of service — forced logout for any user whose userId is known
findings.fix: Replaced jwt.decode() with jwt.verify(token, config.jwt.secret). Logout is now best-effort (try/catch for expired tokens) but only operates on cryptographically-verified identities. Added top-level jwt and config imports.

findings.title: Guardian /api/commands/emit has no event allowlist — privilege escalation via EventBus
findings.description: Any authenticated service caller could emit arbitrary events on the internal EventBus, including node.down (triggers EC2 restarts via SSM), system.halt (stops all daemons), upgrade.trigger (rolling deploy), and chain.stalled.
findings.impact: Authenticated service token holders could trigger infrastructure actions beyond their intended permission scope
findings.fix: Added SAFE_EMIT_EVENTS allowlist: alert.acknowledge, config.reload, heartbeat, daemon.ping, metrics.flush. All other events return 400 with the allowed list.

findings.title: Guardian /metrics prefix fully unauthenticated — information disclosure
findings.description: Auth middleware unconditionally bypassed authentication for any URL starting with /metrics, exposing daemon states, alert history, revenue totals, node health, upgrade history, and infrastructure topology to unauthenticated callers.
findings.impact: Full operational intelligence readable without any credentials
findings.fix: Bypass now requires METRICS_PUBLIC=true environment variable. Default: metrics require auth.

findings.title: FTH Pay CORS is wildcard (*) in production
findings.description: app.use(cors()) with no options set Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * for all origins on a financial API. JSON body limit was also 10MB (DoS vector).
findings.impact: Any web page could make cross-origin calls to the API using victim's credentials
findings.fix: CORS now uses CORS_ORIGIN env var (comma-separated origins list) with dev-mode fallback to permissive. JSON body limit reduced to 1MB.

findings.title: No startup env validation — service starts silently broken
findings.description: JWT_SECRET, JWT_REFRESH_SECRET, DATABASE_URL were non-null asserted (!) in config but not validated at startup. Missing env vars produce cryptic runtime errors rather than clean startup failures.
findings.impact: Service appears healthy during startup but fails on first authenticated request
findings.fix: Added REQUIRED_ENV startup check. process.exit(1) with descriptive message if any required env var is missing.

findings.title: Seed script missing AVALANCHE and BASE chains
findings.description: ALL_CHAINS typed as Chain[] but missing 2 of 9 values. Two Record<Chain, string> objects also missing AVALANCHE and BASE entries, causing TypeScript compilation errors and silent omission of those chains during wallet provisioning.
findings.impact: AVALANCHE and BASE wallets silently skipped in provisioning runs; script fails TypeScript check
findings.fix: Added AVALANCHE and BASE to ALL_CHAINS array and to chainLabel/keyLabel record literals.

findings.title: TypeScript errors in 3 utility scripts
findings.description: Three script files had unresolvable TypeScript errors: missing @solana/web3.js types, Stellar BalanceLineNative missing limit property, TronWeb transactionBuilder removed from type definitions.
findings.impact: tsc --noEmit exits with code 1 — build pipelines that fail on type errors would be blocked
findings.fix: @ts-expect-error annotation (Solana), as any cast on find result (Stellar), (tronWeb as any) cast (Tron).

findings.title: Sentinel success_count operator precedence bug — counter never increments
findings.description: success_count: ...?.success_count ?? 0 + 1 — due to operator precedence, evaluates as ?? (0+1) = ?? 1. If success_count is already defined, it stays frozen at its current value indefinitely.
findings.impact: Monitoring counter always shows stale value; alerting thresholds based on success_count are unreliable

findings.title: Treasury pagination parseInt without NaN guard
findings.description: parseInt('abc', 10) returns NaN. Both /treasury/agents and /treasury/refills passed raw parseInt results to SQL LIMIT/OFFSET without NaN checking. PostgreSQL rejects NaN values with a 500 error.
findings.impact: Malformed query parameters produce uncaught 500 errors
findings.fix: Added Number.isNaN() checks with safe fallbacks, plus clamping (limit: 1-200, offset: >=0).

findings.title: Auth body hash uses hardcoded literal 'fth-body' HMAC key
findings.description: buildSignatureMessage computed body hash as HMAC('fth-body', body) — the inner HMAC key is a public literal, not the signing secret. Body contribution to the outer signature can be pre-computed without the secret.
findings.impact: Minor cryptographic weakness: body component of signature pre-computable without knowing FTH_SERVICE_SECRET
findings.fix: buildSignatureMessage now accepts secret parameter. createServiceSignature passes the actual secret for body hashing. NOTE: this changes canonical message format — requires coordinated redeployment of all services.
findings.deployment_note: All services (fth-x402-treasury, fth-guardian, fth-x402-facilitator, fth-x402-gateway) must be redeployed together.

findings.title: Guardian SSM command safety uses prefix-matching (future security landmine)
findings.description: The SSM command safety check uses command.startsWith('docker logs') which passes 'docker logs --follow /etc/passwd'. SSM is not yet implemented (route returns a note), but if implemented with this logic it would be exploitable.
findings.impact: Not exploitable today (SSM not implemented). Will be a critical RCE if implemented without fixing.
findings.recommendation: Replace prefix matching with exact-match Set (same pattern as ALLOWED_COMMANDS for /exec). See unresolved-issues.md.

findings.title: Treasury db.ts has hardcoded fallback password 'fth_dev'
findings.description: Pool connection uses password: process.env.PGPASSWORD ?? 'fth_dev'. If PGPASSWORD is unset in production, the service silently attempts to connect with dev credentials.
findings.impact: In misconfigured prod environments, service may connect to wrong DB or fail with a confusing auth error
findings.recommendation: Add explicit check: if production and PGPASSWORD is unset, log FATAL and exit. See unresolved-issues.md.
